transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-09-28
- Time: 16:00 PT
- Duration: ~46 mins
- Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Dr. Elena Morales (Sagewell), Arjun Patel (Sagewell Eng), Sofia Ruiz (Sagewell Security)

Auto-summary: Quick walkthrough of Redwood hosted API for embeddings and a lightweight reranker flow. Demonstrated call examples, Console trace for latency/cost, and discussed security/compliance and pilot next steps.

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Jordan with Redwood Inference. With me is Priya, our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:10] Elena: Hi Jordan, good thanks. Excited to see how this could help search in clinical notes.
[00:15] Jordan: Awesome. Real quick run through agenda: embeddings endpoint demo, then a reranker pipeline example, peek at the Console + Optimize suggestions, and then security and next steps. Sound good?
[00:28] Arjun: Yep, sounds good. We're particularly focused on relevance for clinical search and latency under 200ms for rescoring topK.
[00:36] Priya: Great. I'll share my screen and start with the embeddings endpoint example. We're using the hosted API so you don't need to provision infra.
[00:45] [screen share starts] Priya: On the docs page you can see the embeddings API - simple POST to /v1/embeddings with model param. For Sagewell we'd typically recommend a dense-embedding model tuned for clinical text; we have curated model profiles in the catalog.
[01:05] Elena: When you say catalog, is that curated open models or household models? Sorry, heard catalogue.
[01:10] Priya: Sorry, yeah catalog — curated open models. We surface performance profiles so you can pick based on latency or vector dimensionality.
[01:18] Priya: Example request... sending the text snippet, we get back a 1,536-d vector (example), then we persist that in your vector DB. For hosted setups, many customers export to Milvus, Pinecone, or in-house vector store.
[01:33] Arjun: For compliance we plan to store vectors on our side in a VPC subnet — does Redwood support private egress?
[01:40] Jordan: Yes, Redwood Hosted supports private VPC peering for data egress and we have dedicated flows for Redwood Private; for hosted we can do VPC egress or you can ingest vectors into your DB directly. We'll send the VPC peering docs after.
[01:51] Sofia: And about data retention — are request logs kept? Are embeddings persisted on Redwood?
[01:55] Jordan: By default the hosted API is configured to not persist customer payloads beyond short-term logs needed for debugging; we offer options for stricter retention and dedicated instances for longer contracts. We'll add exact retention settings to the notes.
[02:08] Priya: Moving to rerank: typical flow is 1) retrieve topK from your vector DB using embedding similarity, 2) call Redwood's reranker endpoint with query + topK candidates and get back a score or reordered list.
[02:22] [02:22] Priya: I'm showing a live demo with a sample clinical query: 'post-op infection signs after knee arthroplasty' — the retrieve step returns 50 candidates, we then call /v1/rerank with the query and doc snippets.
[02:36] [02:36] Speaker 1 (auto): reranker request payload example...
[02:40] Priya: The reranker can return either a full sorted list or per-candidate scores; you can set max_tokens low since it's mostly classification-like scoring, so token costs are small.
[02:51] Arjun: What's your end-to-end latency for a rerank of topK=50? We need med latency <=200ms in prod.
[02:58] Priya: It depends on model choice and batch. For a mid-size rerank model and continuous batching the p95 for topK 50 is often around 120-180ms in our hosted benchmark; if you want hard SLAs, we recommend Dedicated reserved capacity so you can pin GPU pools.
[03:16] Elena: If we go hosted can we set a latency SLO?
[03:20] Jordan: Hosted has latency targets by model tier but not contract-level SLA unless you buy a dedicated plan. That said, we can recommend model choices and batching configs to hit your 200ms goal.
[03:32] Sofia: Security — do you have SOC2 and KMS/HSM integrations? Our security team requires an HSM-backed key for any exported artifacts.
[03:41] Jordan: Yes, Redwood is SOC2 Type II and supports customer-managed keys via KMS integrations; for Private deployments we can do on-prem HSMs. We'll send SOC2 cert and KMS integration guide.
[03:54] Priya: Switching to Console: here's a trace for a rerank call — you can see token-level cost, model selection, and kernel-level latency. Optimize will flag suggestions like "reduce topK to 30" or "enable prefix KV caching for common queries" to save cost.
[04:12] [04:12] Elena: Is that Optimize suggestions automated? How does it avoid hurting relevance?
[04:18] Priya: Optimize suggests conservative changes and links them to an eval set if you provide a small labeled prompt set. You can preview quality delta on that set before applying.
[04:28] Arjun: For rerank, what's the recommended topK to balance recall vs latency?
[04:32] Priya: Usually 20—50 for enterprise search; we suggest starting at 50 for recall, then use reranker confidence to cut down to 20 in production to save cost and latency. Optimize can run an A/B to measure deltas.
[04:45] Sofia: Do you support audit logs for every inference request? We need retention for 365 days for our audit team.
[04:52] Jordan: Yes, audit logs are available as an add-on with configurable retention; default is 90 days but we can extend to 365 for enterprise. Logs include request metadata and model versions, redacted payloads if requested.
[05:05] Elena: Quick clarifying question — you mentioned KV cache earlier. In clinical search we often have long context snippets; how does KV cache help here?
[05:13] Priya: KV cache speeds up autoregressive generation primarily; for rerank it's less relevant unless you do multi-stage generation. But we do have prefix caching for repeated prefixes in rerank prompts which can reduce compute. Sorry sometimes our docs say KV cache but for rerank it's prefix reuse.
[05:29] Arjun: Any examples you can share for the rerank prompt? We worry about hallucination and preserving factual snippets.
[05:35] Priya: Sure — rerank prompt pattern: include query, short instruction, then numbered candidate passages with metadata fields, ask the model to output a score between 0-1 or a rank. Keep candidates concise and include source ids so you can trace back. We have example templates in the quickstart.
[05:51] [05:51] Jordan: I also want to highlight cost accounting — Console shows per-request token cost and per-model cost. For rerank, since tokens per candidate are small, the unit cost is mostly model compute and topK multiplier.
[06:05] Elena: We're also comparing to a plan of running rerank locally with a fine-tuned model on our GPUs. Where does Redwood fit vs self-host?
[06:12] Jordan: Good question. If you want full control and air-gapped ops, go Private or on-prem. Self-hosting gives control but increases ops burden. Redwood Hosted gives fast time-to-value and predictable per-call unit economics and you avoid maintenance. Dedicated gives the middle ground with reserved capacity and better latency SLAs.
[06:27] Arjun: Regarding throughput, if we run high QPS, is autoscaling immediate? We expect bursts during morning handoffs.
[06:34] Priya: For hosted, we have autoscaling and warm pools; depending on model and concurrency, cold starts are rare, but for strict throughput you can commit to Dedicated with burst capacity.
[06:44] Sofia: Any certifications around HIPAA? We're handling PHI in clinical notes.
[06:48] Jordan: We do have customers in regulated spaces and can discuss HIPAA arrangements with an enterprise contract. For PHI, often customers choose Private or Dedicated with VPC and strict key management. We'll flag this for legal and security follow-up.
[07:05] Priya: Back to a quick live trace — I'm running a rerank of topK 30 now. You can see the trace: total request 145ms, model compute 110ms, network 20ms, serialization 15ms. p95 on this trace is 190ms.
[07:25] [07:25] Elena: Those numbers look promising. Would you be able to run the same on our anonymized dataset? That would be the best proof.
[07:32] Jordan: Absolutely. For benchmarking we usually take a 10k sample, run retrieval + rerank offline and report p50/p95 and relevance metrics (MRR/NDCG). Priya will own the benchmark plan.
[07:45] Priya: I'll need a sample format — ideally JSONL with {id, text, metadata}. I'll send the template. Also indicate whether you want us to call your vector DB or if you want to export candidate lists.
[07:58] Arjun: We can export topK lists. We'll prepare an anonymized 10k sample.
[08:04] Sofia: On the legal side, we need to see SOC2 and details on KMS. Jordan, you said you'd send docs?
[08:09] Jordan: Yes, I'll share SOC2 report and KMS/HSM integration notes after this call.
[08:16] [08:16] Priya: Quick note: if you want to optimize for cost, Console's Optimize recommends quantization candidates and model swaps for similar quality. For rerank we often recommend a two-stage model: smaller, faster model to prune to N, then a larger model for final sort.
[08:31] Elena: That two-stage sounds reasonable. We worry about consistency across time as models update. How do you handle model versioning?
[08:39] Priya: You can pin model versions in the API call or use model aliasing. Console shows model drift and we support rollouts/canary testing so you can test a new model on a percentage of traffic. Rollbacks are built-in.
[08:54] Arjun: For integration, what SDKs do you provide? We use Python backend (FastAPI) and Node on frontend.
[08:59] Jordan: We have Python and Node SDKs, plus curl examples. We'll send code snippets for the rerank flow that plug into FastAPI.
[09:06] Elena: Any gating on the hosted plan for medical customers? We need contractual clauses.
[09:11] Jordan: For PHI and certain regulatory needs we recommend Dedicated or Private. Hosted can be configured but often contract terms and DPA are required. Our sales/legal team will coordinate.
[09:22] Sofia: Can you confirm if payloads are encrypted in transit and at rest with customer-managed keys?
[09:28] Jordan: In transit is TLS; at rest we support customer-managed keys via cloud KMS for any persisted artifacts on Dedicated/Private. For hosted short-lived logs we can encrypt and rotate keys per your policy.
[09:41] [09:41] Priya: Demo wrap-up: here's the code for a rerank call, and here's Console showing cost and an Optimize suggestion to reduce topK from 50 to 30 for a small quality delta.
[09:55] Elena: This has been helpful. Next steps for us: prepare anonymized data and finalize compliance checklist.
[09:59] Jordan: Great — recap of action items: Jordan will share SOC2 + KMS docs and pricing/quickstart; Priya will send benchmark plan and data template; Sagewell will prepare anonymized 10k sample and compliance questions. We'll schedule a follow-up in two weeks to review benchmark results.
[10:18] Arjun: One last quick question — do you throttle calls per org or per token? If we exceed usage, is there graceful degradation?
[10:24] Jordan: We use rate limits and quotas per API key/org; for Hosted we also have fallback policies to a lower-cost model and automatic backpressure signals. Those policies are configurable.
[10:36] Elena: Thanks everyone. Looking forward to the benchmark.
[10:40] Jordan: Thanks all — we'll follow up with docs and the benchmark plan.

Transcript notes: occasional auto-attributions and filler words. Some technical terms auto-transcribed (e.g., "KV cache" vs "prefix cache"). References shared: quickstart code link (sent in chat), SOC2 PDF (to be sent), benchmark template (to be sent).

End of transcript.
